newsitem.title: AUSTRIA: Austria begins budget talks for 1998/99.
newsitem.headline: Austria begins budget talks for 1998/99.

text.p: Austria on Tuesday began negotiations over the budgets for 1998 and 1999 that should build on the foundations already laid out for the country's early entry into Europe's single currency union.

The last two budgets, for 1996 and 1997, were hammered out after months of political wrangling between the Social Democrats and their junior coalition partner conservative People's Party. Agreement was only reached after a snap general election.
The coalition government has forecast an overall budget deficit at no more than 3.0 percent this year, down from about 4.0 percent last year.

Last month, Finance Minister Rudolf Edlinger said that based on 1997 budget projections, he was confident that Austria would qualify for the single currency and vowed to maintain a tight grip on public spending in the coming years.
Austria takes on the rotating presidency of the European Union in the second half of 1998.
